The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `da2bf989f2c1e1c2dc52870a47732564b38b4f74`, but the prepared workspace source used for the saved crash is the staged commit above, which still contains the unfixed `consumeTerm()` backslash case shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42487554 (hermes): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target fuzzer-jsi-entry [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42487554
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 27-byte JavaScript witness `60 60 2e 6d 61 74 63 68 60`, fifteen `20` bytes, `5c 5c 60` calls `String.prototype.match` as a tag with one template element whose cooked string is fifteen spaces followed by a single trailing backslash. `stringPrototypeMatch()` creates a new RegExp from that argument, `JSRegExp::initialize()` appends the pattern into stack `patternText16`, and `Regex<UTF16RegexTraits>::parse()` builds a parser with `current_`/`end_` spanning those 16 UTF-16 code units. Inside one `consumeTerm()` invocation, the default arm `re_->pushChar(consume(c));` iterates over the fifteen spaces and advances `current_` to the final backslash. The next loop iteration enters `case '\\'`, `consume('\\')` advances `current_` to `end_`, and the code immediately evaluates `*current_ == 'b' || *current_ == 'B'` without checking `current_ == end_`. That dereferences one `char16_t` past the pattern buffer and produces the saved AddressSanitizer `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at `RegexParser.cpp:423`; ASan identifies the overrun object as `patternText16` in `JSRegExp::initialize()`. The fix inserts the missing `current_ == end_` check and returns `EscapeIncomplete` instead of reading beyond the regex text.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled regex pattern into the UTF-16 buffer later parsed by `RegexParser`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 27 ASCII bytes: `60 60 2e 6d 61 74 63 68 60`, then fifteen `20` bytes, then `5c 5c 60`. In Hermes this is an empty template literal followed by `.match` used as a tagged template with one element, so the cooked pattern string reaching this line is fifteen spaces plus a single trailing backslash.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Immediately after consuming a backslash, `consumeTerm()` dereferences `*current_` without checking whether `current_` has reached `end_`. When the pattern ends in a lone backslash, the missing guard turns the intended `EscapeIncomplete` error path into an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (current_ == end_) { setError(constants::ErrorType::EscapeIncomplete); return; }` at this exact site.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. With `current_ == end_`, evaluating this branch dereferences one `char16_t` past the regex pattern buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 2` at this line and identifies `patternText16` in `JSRegExp::initialize()` as the overflowed stack object.

parser_admitted.description: The JavaScript source has already evaluated far enough that `String.prototype.match` is constructing a new RegExp from the attacker-controlled tagged-template argument.

pattern_string_normalized.description: Before `JSRegExp::initialize()` copies the pattern into `patternText16`, the tagged-template argument is normalized into the `StringPrimitive` passed as `P`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The UTF-16 regex text buffer later traversed by `current_`. For the saved witness it contains sixteen code units: fifteen spaces and a final backslash.
tainted_value_origin.note: `appendUTF16String()` appends exactly `getStringLength()` code units and no terminator, so the parser must rely on `end_` as the only bound.

coarse_trace.summary: The tagged-template `.match` call reaches `String.prototype.match`, which creates a new RegExp from the attacker-controlled template argument and normalizes it to the pattern string ending in a lone backslash.
`JSRegExp::initialize()` copies that pattern into stack `patternText16`, and the regex parser captures a `[current_, end_)` range over those sixteen UTF-16 code units.

Within one `consumeTerm()` invocation, fifteen default-arm iterations `re_->pushChar(consume(c));` consume the space prefix and advance `current_` to the terminal backslash; the next loop iteration loads that last code unit and enters the backslash arm.

That backslash arm executes `consume('\\')`, leaves `current_ == end_`, and then immediately evaluates `*current_` without the missing `current_ == end_` guard, producing the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ on `patternText16`.

fine_trace.note: Source. This stack buffer receives the regex text that ASan later reports as overrun. For the saved witness it holds sixteen UTF-16 code units: fifteen spaces and a final backslash. `appendUTF16String()` appends exactly the string length and no sentinel, so later parser reads are bounded only by `end_`.

The parser snapshots a half-open range over step 1's buffer: `current_` starts at the first code unit and `end_` points one past the trailing backslash. This `end_` iterator is the only bound that should protect later `*current_` reads.

Inside the `consumeTerm()` call reached from `performParse()`/`consumeDisjunction()`, the first fifteen loop iterations see `c == ' '`, take this default arm, and execute `consume(c)` on each ordinary space. Those repeated in-bounds consumes advance `current_` from the start of `patternText16` to the sixteenth code unit, the terminal backslash.
The first read inside `consumeTerm()` is still in-bounds: it loads the last pattern code unit into `c`. For this witness `c` is `'\\'`, so the switch enters the backslash escape arm.

In the backslash case, `consume()` asserts the current character matches and then executes `current_++` (line 136). Because this is the pattern's last code unit, that increment moves `current_` from the trailing backslash to exactly `end_`.

Root cause. After step 5, `current_` already equals `end_`, but the vulnerable backslash arm falls through to this `if` without checking that condition. The fix adds `if (current_ == end_) { setError(constants::ErrorType::EscapeIncomplete); return; }` here instead of letting execution proceed to the dereference.

Sink. Evaluating the left side `*current_ == 'b'` dereferences a `char16_t` at `end_`, one code unit past `patternText16`. AddressSanitizer reports this as `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this exact line and identifies `patternText16` as the overrun stack object.

allocation_context.note: AddressSanitizer identifies local stack object `patternText16` as occupying `[224,272)` in this frame and reports the invalid read at offset 272, one `char16_t` past that object.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run feeds the exact staged 27-byte JavaScript program `60 60 2e 6d 61 74 63 68 60`, fifteen `20` bytes, `5c 5c 60` to `fuzzer-jsi-entry` and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `hermes::regex::Parser<...>::consumeTerm`; the program reaches `String.prototype.match` with a regex pattern string of fifteen spaces plus a lone trailing backslash.

format.name: JavaScript source
format.contract: Exactly the staged 27-byte JavaScript source in `poc` (sha256 `326118b4e0b3cf78452c6d765a869093a60774d5700ea9e692a3766b2d4aefda`): `60 60 2e 6d 61 74 63 68 60`, fifteen `20` bytes, `5c 5c 60`. Its verified trigger semantics are limited to the path this witness takes: Hermes evaluates the tagged-template `.match` form so `String.prototype.match` constructs a RegExp whose parser stays in `Parser::consumeTerm()`'s main loop, consumes the fifteen leading spaces via the default arm `re_->pushChar(consume(c));`, and then enters `case '\\'` with `current_` on the final UTF-16 code unit and `end_` immediately after it. In the saved witness the template's cooked pattern string is fifteen spaces plus one trailing backslash; this GT does not generalize to other trailing-backslash contexts such as bracket-class parsing.
